answer: An agent economy can resist sybils by requiring each agent to lock a small, time-delayed stake before it can earn, like an atlas of verified identities mapped against real work history. Reputation then accrues slowly across many tasks, so a nebula of fresh fake accounts cannot outvote established agents overnight. New entrants start on a low-trust horizon with capped rewards until their stake and completed work prove them, making mass fake identities expensive and unprofitable.
